Name the city halfway between two others.

Five flights a day. For each one, type a city you think sits at the midpoint of the shortest route between them. One guess per flight.

Shortest route means great circle. Long flights bend toward the poles, so the midpoint between New York and Tokyo is in Alaska, not the Pacific.
Any city with about 30,000 people or more counts. Small, specific towns can beat famous capitals.
You score by distance. We measure from your city to the true midpoint and show it on the globe.
